widgets.name: kl-policy-explorer
widgets.teaching_point: The KL-regularised optimum pi* = pi_ref exp(r / beta) / Z: beta trades expected reward against distance from the reference, and a small beta lets the policy exploit any error in the reward.
controls: slider: beta from 0.02 to 20, log scale, default 1.0
eight reward sliders r_1..r_8 from -3 to 3, step 0.1
eight reference-probability inputs (renormalised automatically; each clamped to at least 1e-6) and a preset menu: 'default', 'uniform reference', 'best response is rare'
toggle: proxy mode (response 8 gets proxy reward 2.0 but true reward -1.0, a reward-model error)
button: sweep beta from 20 down to 0.02 over 4 seconds
pair picker: choose two responses w and l
displays: bar chart of pi_ref (outlined grey bars) and pi* (filled bars) for y1..y8, rewards printed under the bars
readouts: KL(pi* || pi_ref) in nats, E_pi*[r], E_pi_ref[r], the objective E[r] - beta KL, beta log Z (always equal to the objective), entropy of pi*
frontier plot: E_pi*[r] against KL(pi* || pi_ref) traced over 200 log-spaced beta values, with the current beta as a dot; in proxy mode a second curve for the true reward that rises and then falls
implicit-reward panel: beta log(pi* / pi_ref) for each response beside r - beta log Z, identical by construction
pair panel: sigma(r_w - r_l) and the implicit-reward margin beta log(pi*(w) / pi_ref(w)) - beta log(pi*(l) / pi_ref(l)), equal to r_w - r_l at the optimum
widgets.spec: Compute in log space: l_i = log pi_ref_i + r_i / beta; m = max_i l_i; Z' = sum_i exp(l_i - m); pi*_i = exp(l_i - m) / Z'; beta log Z = beta (m + log Z'). KL = sum_i pi*_i (log pi*_i - log pi_ref_i), skipping terms with pi*_i < 1e-300; E[r] = sum_i pi*_i r_i; entropy = -sum pi* log pi*. The frontier uses 200 beta values log-spaced from 20 to 0.02 and recomputes on any reward or reference change. Proxy mode: r_proxy = r with r_8 = 2.0 forced, r_true = r with r_8 = -1.0; pi* uses r_proxy; the frontier draws E[r_proxy] and E[r_true]. Reference values at the defaults: beta = 0.5 gives KL 0.899 and E[r] 1.275; beta = 0.25 gives KL 2.378; as beta -> 0, pi* collapses on y8 and KL -> -ln 0.03 = 3.507. In proxy mode E[r_true] is 0.316 under pi_ref, peaks at 0.454 near beta = 0.90 (KL 0.27), is 0.331 at beta = 0.5 and -0.347 at beta = 0.25, and tends to -1.0. Edge cases: equal rewards give pi* = pi_ref and KL = 0; ties at the maximum reward split mass in proportion to pi_ref as beta -> 0; inputs are validated (numbers only). Vanilla JS with SVG or canvas; accessible labels on sliders; works at 400 px width by stacking the panels.

widgets.name: grpo-group-explorer
widgets.teaching_point: GRPO's advantage is a reward standardised within the group: groups that are all right or all wrong teach nothing, and the share of informative groups depends on the pass rate and the group size.
controls: slider: group size G from 2 to 16 (integer), default 8
a row of G reward cells: click to toggle 0/1 in binary mode, or drag a 0-1 slider per cell in partial-credit mode
toggle: divide by the group standard deviation (on, as in GRPO) or not (Dr. GRPO)
toggle: unbiased (n - 1) or population standard deviation
slider: pass rate p from 0 to 1, step 0.01, with a button 'resample group from Bernoulli(p)'
optional per-sample length inputs in tokens (default 200 each)
displays: signed bar chart of the advantages A_i with the group mean and standard deviation drawn as reference lines
readouts: mean, standard deviation, sum of advantages (always 0), number of non-zero advantages, and the message 'no gradient: every sample got the same reward' when the variance is zero
per-token weight bars A_i / |y_i| (GRPO) beside A_i / max_len (constant normaliser) when lengths differ
curve of P(group carries signal) = 1 - p^G - (1 - p)^G against p for the current G, with G = 4 and G = 16 as faint references and the current p marked
leave-one-out panel: r_i minus the mean of the other G - 1 rewards, and the factor (G - 1) / G relating it to r_i minus the group mean
widgets.defaults: G = 8, binary mode, rewards (1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0), std on (unbiased), p = 0.5, all lengths 200. The chart shows +2.475 for the correct sample and -0.354 for each other; the signal curve shows 0.992 at p = 0.5.
widgets.spec: Advantages follow the source's code: mean = average of rewards; std = sample standard deviation (divide by G - 1) unless the population toggle is on; if std == 0 every advantage is 0; otherwise A_i = (r_i - mean) / (std + 1e-6), or r_i - mean when the std toggle is off. Reference values: one correct of 8 gives +2.475 / -0.354; two correct give +1.620 / -0.540; four give +/-0.935; G = 2 with (1, 0) gives +/-0.707; partial credit (0.9, 0.5, 0.5, 0.0, 0.2, 0.0, 0.7, 0.3) gives (1.588, 0.349, 0.349, -1.201, -0.581, -1.201, 0.969, -0.271). The signal curve is sampled at 101 points; at G = 8 it reads 0.149, 0.570, 0.992, 0.570, 0.337 at p = 0.02, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.95. Resampling draws G Bernoulli(p) rewards with a seeded generator shown on screen. Length panel: with lengths 200 and 800 and A = -0.6 the per-token weights are -0.003 and -0.00075. Edge cases: changing G keeps existing cells and fills new ones with 0; all partial-credit values equal gives zero advantages. Vanilla JS, SVG, keyboard-operable cells.

writer_notes:
GENERAL. This outline is the contract between six writers. Keep notation, running examples and numbers exactly as given; where a number is marked 'our run' it comes from a prototype run of the lab code (CPU, 4 threads, torch 2.14, transformers 5.18, fixed seeds) and will be replaced by the executed output in a later phase, so phrase the prose so that the last digits can change ('about 0.74').

NOTATION (use throughout). pi_theta: the policy being trained; pi_ref: the reference (the SFT model, or the base with the adapter switched off under LoRA); beta: the KL coefficient, the same symbol and meaning in RLHF, DPO and GRPO (example values: 0.05 in Section 6's sequence-reward example, 0.1 for DPO, 0.04 for GRPO); r_phi: a learned reward; r or r*: a true or generic reward; y_w, y_l: chosen and rejected; log pi(y|x): the sum of token log-probabilities over the assistant tokens including the end-of-turn token; Z(x): the partition function; rho: the importance ratio; A or A_i: advantage; epsilon: clip range; G: group size; sigma: the logistic function; KL in nats. N is the total parameter count (memory, Chinchilla); N_matmul = N - V d is the count that does arithmetic (FLOPs, Module 06). LoRA's factors are matrices, bold A and bold B as the series' notation requires; the batch size is the italic scalar B (BRIEF), and the bootstrap's number of resamples is written in words ('10,000 resamples'), never as B. Standard deviations in GRPO are the unbiased (n - 1) estimator, matching torch.std's default and the source's code; all worked GRPO numbers use it.

UNITS, FLOPS, HARDWARE AND PRICES. Memory in decimal GB (10^9 bytes), stated once in Section 4, as in Modules 07, 08 and 10; GPU capacities are marketed sizes (24, 48, 80 GB), about 24 GiB = 25.8 GB for a 24 GB card. FLOPs follow Module 06's convention, stated once in Section 4 with a link and never re-derived: forward 2 N_matmul per token plus attention (4Ldt at context t, averaging 2LdT over a causal sequence of length T); training three times the forward, 6 N_matmul + 6LTd; LoRA 4 N_matmul + 6LTd (the matmuls' weight gradients are skipped, attention's backward is not). Case study: forward 2 N_matmul = 1.79e10 per token before attention; training 5.36e10 + 7.25e9 (+13.5%) = 6.08e10 per token at T = 8,192; LoRA 4.30e10. Do not write 2N, 4N or 6N with the total count unless it is labelled a +7% estimate.
